subtype: Making own bag, bed and simple food [Actor]
passage: In the hill village, Pema had packed her school bag the night before, with the copybooks in the order of the timetable. Now, in the cold morning, she pulled her blanket straight and folded it into a square, the way Ama did. It took longer than she thought. Then Jatin, her father, lit the wood stove and stood beside her while she measured tea leaves into the pot and watched the water. He held the handle of the pot when it came time to pour. "Careful, it's hot." Pema carried her cup with both hands to the step and blew on it. She looked back at the room, and wondered how Ama did all of this every day.

qa.q: What did Pema do the night before school?
qa.a: Pema packed her school bag with the copybooks in the order of the timetable.

qa.q: What was Pema thinking and feeling as she looked back at the room?
qa.a: Pema was surprised and a little admiring, wondering how her mother managed all this work every day.

qa.q: What made it safe for Pema to make tea?
qa.a: Her father Jatin stood beside her, lit the stove and held the handle of the hot pot when it was time to pour.

qa.q: How might Jatin feel watching Pema measure the tea leaves?
qa.a: Jatin is probably proud and watchful at once, staying close to keep her safe while letting her do the job.

grounding: Shows a schoolchild packing her bag, making the bed and preparing tea under supervision and noticing how much home work exists.

subtype: Making own bag, bed and simple food [Actor]
passage: Saturday morning in Prague, ten-year-old Jana was making her own sandwich for the school trip. Her father Javier stood by the counter with a cup of coffee. She buttered the bread, laid on cheese, and sliced a cucumber with the small knife, slowly, the way he had shown her, fingers curled. It took ten minutes, and she left a trail of crumbs. Then she wrapped it, put it in her bag with a water bottle and a jumper, and zipped the bag. She glanced at the pile of dishes she had used. "Papa, is this how much work you do every day?" Javier laughed. "And that was only one sandwich."

qa.q: What did Jana slice with the small knife?
qa.a: Jana sliced a cucumber with the small knife.

qa.q: What was Jana thinking when she glanced at the pile of dishes?
qa.a: Jana was surprised and impressed at how much work one small task made, and it led her to ask about the work Papa does every day.

qa.q: What made it safe for Jana to use the knife?
qa.a: Javier stood by the counter and had shown her how to slice slowly with fingers curled.

qa.q: What might Javier feel when Jana asks if this is how much work he does?
qa.a: Javier probably feels amused and moved, since Jana has noticed the daily work that usually goes unseen.

grounding: Shows a schoolchild making a simple sandwich and packing her bag under supervision, gaining awareness of how much home work exists.
